$comment: EXPERIMENTAL — declarative mapping from the canonical Part IV instance-data model (criterion C31, slc-stand-to-spec-avg) to the UBL QualificationApplicationREQUEST XML — the BUYER/CONTRACTING-AUTHORITY side. This is the first mapping in the model to target the REQUEST document and the buyer's `requirement` sub-object, closing the 'request side' gap noted in docs/model-xml-mapping.md. Only the `requirement` sub-object is mapped here; the economic operator's `response` maps to the response document (part-IV.response.mapping.json). Same engine and `records` construct as the response side: each buyer requirement is a cac:TenderingCriterionProperty keyed by its property id (the EDM `responsepath`, …/R1) and carrying an Expected*/Minimum* value.

$notes.requirementRecords: A REQUIREMENT in the request is a cac:TenderingCriterionProperty whose cbc:ID identifies the property and whose body is an Expected*/Minimum* element (NOT a cac:TenderingCriterionResponse — that is the response document). We reuse the generic `records` construct: the wrapper is cac:TenderingCriterionProperty, the key is cbc:ID (schemeID='criterion'), and each body is a typed `value`. The engine hardcodes none of these names.
$notes.expectedElements: Per the EA criterion definition and the ESPD examples, the Expected element is dictated by the requirement's ValueDataTypeCode: QUANTITY_YEAR -> cbc:ExpectedValueNumeric; DESCRIPTION -> cbc:ExpectedDescription; MINIMUM_AMOUNT -> cbc:MinimumAmount (with a currencyID attribute). The buyer's minimum amount is a MINIMUM_AMOUNT datatype, hence cbc:MinimumAmount rather than cbc:ExpectedAmount.
$notes.amount: The minimum-amount currency is a data-sourced attribute (cbc:MinimumAmount@currencyID from requirement.minimumAmount.currency), so it roundtrips — the same value-attribute { from } pattern used for the response amount.
$notes.keyForm: Property ids use the EDM `responsepath` form (…/R1), the value the Schematron matches with schemeID='criterion'. When per-property UUIDs are available upstream only these key strings change.

rules.$comment: C31 criterion declaration — criterion UUID (from the EA export). Pure constant metadata: no instance-data home, not written back on import.

RG1/RQ1 — LOT Identifier(s) (LOT_IDENTIFIER, 1..n). Selection criteria are lot-specific (Schematron BR-LOT-40). Scalar-item `records` form: one cac:TenderingCriterionProperty per lot id, all sharing the fixed key `…/RG1/RQ1/R1`, each carrying one cbc:ExpectedID. On import the lots are rebuilt from the records carrying this key, in document order.
Buyer requirement records. Each `entries` item emits one cac:TenderingCriterionProperty with a keyed property id (…/R1) and one Expected*/Minimum* body. Absent optional requirements emit nothing.

entries.$comment: RG1/RSG1/RQ1 — 'Number of fiscal years' (QUANTITY_YEAR). Buyer-set count -> cbc:ExpectedValueNumeric.
RG1/RSG1/RQ2 — 'Business domain description' (DESCRIPTION). Buyer-set text -> cbc:ExpectedDescription.
RG1/RSG1/RQ3 — 'Minimum amount requirement' (MINIMUM_AMOUNT). Buyer threshold -> cbc:MinimumAmount with a data-sourced currencyID attribute.
